name: @olai/tests
//scripts: Bun hosts the runner, and `test` NAMES cucumber's entry file so that it does — never the `cucumber-js` bin, whose `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang is resolved against PATH and hands the suite to whatever node the host has. README.md tells that story; runner.test.ts pins the spelling. Keep it a path: this one is stable because the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) gives every package its own direct dependencies.
//dependencies: @olai/web for the NAMES it owns and nothing else — the `data-testid` record (support/world.ts), the day arithmetic, the deadlines a wait is measured against, the theme table's attribute, storage key and default — reached through its `./testlib` subpath ALONE: the curated door `imports.test.ts` fences, on both ends. @olai/fonts is the same arrangement one package over — the TYPEFACE table's attribute, storage key and default, imported from the package that owns them rather than from the client that draws them. Each is a contract between two packages that never otherwise meet, and the way that kind of contract breaks is silent — a rename compiles on both sides and shows up as a thirty-second timeout. Importing makes it a type error instead. @olai/format is here for two NAMES on the same terms: `MARKS`, the three fields a record may carry, so the disk assertion that a node is UNMARKED is written against the format's own list rather than three field names this suite would spell alone and quietly stop covering the day a fourth arrived — and `FILE_KINDS`, the table saying which files a served directory is made of, so the sweeps in kinds.test.ts hunt the suffixes the format actually claims rather than a list of them kept here. @olai/surface is the same again for the two halves of what a `.html` preview IS on the wire: `mediaHref`, the address a preview frame is pointed at, and `sealPolicy`, the exact content policy the server answers it with — so the scenario that says a preview is sealed reads the policy the server writes rather than a copy of it that could go on passing after the real one was widened. @olai/identity is two names the identity scenarios stand on: the gravatar URL the chip must show — imported so a hash spelled twice cannot disagree, and so the step does not check a URL with an unanchored regex — and the DEFAULT header names a proxy injects (login, display name, picture), so a Given writes the header olai actually reads rather than a copy of its spelling that would go on passing after the default moved. @olai/plugin-api is the same carve-out one wall further out, and the wall is what makes it a carve-out rather than a shortcut: `packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts` holds as an equality per package that nothing outside the registry imports a plugin or declares one, so the padi pill's ids — which are a plugin's output, not the app's — reach this suite through `@olai/plugin-api/testids`. That door is NAMES ONLY, which is the property that matters here: a testid door reaching a COMPONENT would put SolidJS, a terminal emulator and the client's own module-scope dial on the graph of a cucumber process with no browser in it, which is exactly the boot death imports.test.ts was written after. @olai/state is the newest and the same carve-out again: where olai keeps this machine's own files is that package's own decision — a per-kind subdirectory under the state home, named by a digest of the served directory's realpath — and the node-agent scenarios have to WRITE a binding record where the serve will read it. A copy of that rule here would go on writing a file nothing reads, and the scenario would fail thirty seconds later as a timeout with nothing to say about why. NAMES and a PURE READ (a hash), like the rest. No MACHINERY is imported from any of them: the furthest a step goes past a NAME is a PURE READ of the client's own — `fileKind`, `gravatarOf`, `mediaHref`, and the door's own `completingIn` — because these tests drive the client through a browser, and nothing they import may need one.
//devDependencies: @olai/log is here for its `./testlib` DECODER only: the readiness signal this suite waits on is a line on the server's stdout, and that line's format belongs to @olai/log — so the thing that reads it back is @olai/log's too, rather than a regex this suite would maintain alone and silently stop matching the day a value needed quoting. playwright is pinned to 1.61.1 — the version of `pkgs.playwright-driver` in the pinned nixpkgs. The npm package ships only the driver's JS; the browsers come from the Nix store via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, and the driver refuses a browser build it was not compiled against. A minor-version drift here (kolu's 1.59.0, say) does not fail at install time — it fails at `chromium.launch()` with "Executable doesn't exist", pointing at a path inside the store that is real but wrong. Bump this only together with the nixpkgs pin, never on its own.
